chapter_title: Chương 60: 0060 Các Trường Danh Giá Công Khai Tranh Giành Nhân Tài

segments.title: Chương 60: 0060 Các Trường Danh Giá Công Khai Tranh Giành Nhân Tài
segments.content:
The university teachers in the great hall were currently split into two groups.

The professors who had participated in judging the manuscripts during the day were responsible for communicating with the Group B first-prize winners.

The group that had just appeared tonight, however, were all leaders with real power in admissions, responsible for engaging with the Group A first-prize winners.

Nanjing University, for example, had sent a section chief from their admissions office, attending as a representative for the admissions director.

Tsinghua had sent the head of their Chinese department, the very same person who had received Ge Fei's call that morning. He had been waiting for his flight at the time, had only just flown into Shanghai in the mid-afternoon, and had to fly out again tomorrow for other matters.

Fudan had sent the deputy head of their Chinese department, who had driven over from his home in the afternoon.

These people only looked at the essays of the 27 Group A first-prize winners, and from among them, they would pick those they were satisfied with.

They all had their eyes on Chen Guiliang!

Chen Guiliang walked into the hall with the other contestants, not rushing to approach anyone, but carefully surveying which universities were present.

Ten heavyweight universities had come: Tsinghua, Beida, Fudan, Nankai, Wuda, Nanda, Xiada, Zhongshan, Beishida, and Huashida. (University poll at the end of the chapter.)

There were also some arts institutes tagging along, whose winners could go on to study majors like screenwriting.

After getting a clear picture, Chen Guiliang headed straight for Tsinghua.

Two people were already making inquiries at Director Wang of Tsinghua's table. Chen Guiliang wasn't in a hurry and stood to the side, listening to what they were saying.

One winner asked, "Professor Wang, how many points can Tsinghua lower its requirements by this year? And how many spots are there in total?"

Director Wang replied, "We will place the New Concept first-prize winners on Tsinghua's list of high-priority admissions candidates. However, there is no policy for lowering the score requirement for now. If you pass Tsinghua's admission cutoff and list Tsinghua as your first choice, there is a high chance you will be accepted."

This answer wasn't entirely useless.

There were indeed people who barely passed the admission cutoff but were ultimately not accepted by Tsinghua. In such a situation, the New Concept first-prize award would give them an advantage.

Hearing there was no policy for lowering scores, the two winners immediately lost interest.

After a few more words, they bowed and took their leave.

"Chen Guiliang!"

Director Wang from Tsinghua, seeing Chen Guiliang standing nearby, actually called out his name proactively, as if afraid Chen Guiliang wouldn't come over to talk.

"Hello, Director Wang," Chen Guiliang greeted him. "You know me?"

Director Wang smiled. "I saw your ID photo from the competition entry. Are you interested in coming to Tsinghua?"

Chen Guiliang said, "My academic performance is still a bit far from Tsinghua's standards."

"What are your usual test scores?" Director Wang asked.

Chen Guiliang said, "Getting into a second-tier university is no problem, and sometimes I can pass the first-tier cutoff. If I work hard before the Gaokao, I might be able to get into a regular key university."

"Is that so," Director Wang thought for a moment. "Both Professor Liu from Tsinghua and I liked your essay very much. Although we don't have a score-reduction policy at the moment, we can discuss it after the school year begins. As you know, Gaokao admissions are a major affair. It's not something one or two teachers can decide; it must be put to a collective vote in a meeting."

"I understand. Thank you, Director Wang," Chen Guiliang said.

Director Wang said, "Leave me a phone number, and keep your phone on at all times. If the university reaches a decision after discussion, I will notify you one week before the independent admissions exam."

Chen Guiliang wrote down his Xiaolingtong number, then, worried the device wasn't reliable, added Bian Guanyue's cell phone number, with "emergency contact" noted in parentheses.

Director Wang accepted the phone numbers with a smile.

After that brief conversation with Chen Guiliang, Director Wang already had a good sense of the situation. While he couldn't secure a full exam waiver, he believed he could probably apply for extremely favorable terms when the school held its discussion meeting.

For example, if Chen Guiliang's score passed the first-tier or key university cutoff, he could be admitted to Tsinghua through special recruitment.

This kind of thing required effort from both sides. Director Wang would do his best to fight for it, and Chen Guiliang had to do his best on the exam.

Otherwise, no matter how hard Director Wang fought, it would be useless. For someone like Han Han, who failed a heap of high school subjects, Tsinghua would never accept him, no matter how well he wrote.

Just as Chen Guiliang left, another winner stepped forward.

That winner directly picked up the pen on the table, wrote down his family's landline number, and then his head teacher's cell phone number. "Director Wang, I don't have a cell phone, and no one might be home to answer the landline. This is my head teacher's cell phone number. If you can't get through on the landline, you can call this number."

"Well..."

Director Wang swallowed the words on the tip of his tongue and nodded. "Alright, I'll notify you if there's any news. But Tsinghua doesn't have a score-reduction policy. You might want to check out some other universities."

The winner asked, puzzled, "Didn't you just say that Tsinghua would hold another meeting to discuss it?"

Director Wang was at a loss for words. There was no way to explain this. Was he supposed to say they were holding a meeting specifically to make a special admission for Chen Guiliang?

Director Wang said ambiguously, "A meeting might not necessarily lead to a result. You shouldn't get your hopes up too high. How are your usual test scores?"

"I'm consistently above the key university cutoff. If I perform well, I have a shot at Tsinghua, Beida, Fudan, or Jiaotong," the winner said.

Director Wang smiled encouragingly. "Then I wish you an outstanding performance on the Gaokao."

Chen Guiliang had already made his way over to Beida's table.

Beida placed great importance on the New Concept competition and had sent the Head of their Social Sciences Department.

There was a nameplate on the table, clearly stating his name and position.

Chen Guiliang greeted him, "Hello, Head Cheng."

"You must be Chen Guiliang, right? How are your grades usually?" Head Cheng smiled kindly.

Chen Guiliang answered him earnestly.

Head Cheng said, "Your essay was very well-written. This year, Beida is only offering a 20-point reduction for New Concept winners. But if you go through the independent admissions process, I can lower the requirement for you to the key university cutoff score. As long as you pass the key university cutoff, Beida will accept you directly!"

"I'll do my best," Chen Guiliang said.

Afraid that Fudan might snatch him away, Head Cheng added, "Actually, as long as you pass the first-tier cutoff, you'll also have a very high chance. Some things can be flexible; we can discuss it again in a meeting then."

He was ninety percent confident he could get Chen Guiliang approved for admission with a first-tier cutoff score.

But he couldn't make an absolute promise. What if something unexpected happened?

"Thank you, Head Cheng."

"Let's exchange contact information."

As Chen Guiliang was writing down his phone number, the winner standing behind him was dumbfounded.

They were both first-prize winners, so why was this guy getting special treatment?

Once Chen Guiliang left, the person immediately went forward. "Sir, I can easily pass the key university cutoff."

Aside from Chen Guiliang, which of the contestants who dared to inquire at Tsinghua and Beida wasn't confident of passing the key university cutoff?

Head Cheng said, "A 20-point reduction."

"Why is he different? That's not fair!" this winner complained, disgruntled.

Head Cheng said, "After the winning essays are published, you can go and appreciate Chen Guiliang's work."

Chen Guiliang then strolled over to Fudan's table.

"Hello, Director Wang."

"Chen Guiliang, right? How are your grades usually?"

"I'm guaranteed a spot in a second-tier university, aiming for a first-tier."

"Then there's no problem. Come to Fudan. We'll accept you as long as you pass the undergraduate cutoff score."

"What?"

"Even if you only pass the third-tier cutoff score, Fudan will still accept you. Come take the independent admissions exam in March. I'll send you a few past exam papers for you to use as reference."

The number of people inquiring at Fudan's table was much greater than at Tsinghua's or Beida's.

After all, not everyone could get exceptionally high scores.

When Director Wang said, "We'll accept you even with a third-tier score," the other winners were utterly stunned.

Director Yan from Beishida was at the next table. Fearing that Chen Guiliang would be poached, she immediately stood up and walked over. "Chen Guiliang, as long as you take Beishida's independent admissions exam, you can be admitted regardless of your Gaokao score!"

The winners inquiring at Beishida's table were also stunned.

Didn't she just say it was only a 30-point reduction?

"Director Yan, why are you always trying to snatch people from me?" Director Wang said, displeased.

Director Yan said, "We have always valued the New Concept Competition. Last year, we only had 18 independent admission spots, and 7 of them went to New Concept winners. What's wrong with giving out one exam waiver this year?"

Director Wang couldn't be bothered to argue with a woman. He said to Chen Guiliang, "Chen, you can think it over carefully. Fudan's offer is the most suitable for you. Since you're guaranteed to get into a second-tier university and can even aim for a first-tier, a waiver doesn't really matter. You've studied hard for three years in high school and put in so much effort. A waiver would simply be a waste of all that work. Doesn't that make sense?"

Director Yan said, "The Gaokao still has its risks. What if he has an off day and underperforms?"

Director Wang retorted, "He's guaranteed a second-tier spot. Even if he underperforms, is he going to fail to even get a third-tier score? Fudan is only asking him to meet the undergraduate cutoff."

Fudan and Beishida had historically been the two universities with the closest partnership with the New Concept competition.

The leaders sent by these two schools had a great deal of discretionary power over recruiting the winners. They could offer exceptionally generous terms as a special exception without even needing to seek further approval from their superiors.

Director Yan was 40 years old this year, with a chin-length bob and glasses.

Like a caring aunt, she took Chen Guiliang's hand and said, "At Beijing Normal University, we value talented students very highly. We won't just recruit you; after you enter university, we will also pay close attention to your future development. Things like joining the Party, participating in the student union... you'll have preferential treatment in all of these."

Well now, she was even saying things like that.

Chen Guiliang looked overwhelmed with gratitude. "Thank you for your high regard, Director Yan!"

Director Wang grew anxious. "Fudan offers preferential treatment too. Don't you worry, Chen."

Xiamen University and Huazhong Normal University's favorable admissions policies for New Concept winners were second only to Fudan's and Beishida's.

Director Chen from Huashida could no longer sit still. He walked over and said, "Chen, you can come to our university. We also don't look at your Gaokao score, and you can pick any liberal arts major you want. Plus, there's additional preferential treatment after you enroll!"

"Whatever policies Huashida offers, we at Xiamen University can offer too," said Professor Gao from Xiada.

Because these four universities offered the strongest support, they also had the most winners inquiring with them.

At this moment, seeing the four universities openly vying for one person, more than a dozen winners were frozen in a daze.

Mi Lan was by Fudan's table, and Luo Jin was by Beishida's table.

They came together, staring at each other.

"What on earth did Chen Guiliang write?" Luo Jin couldn't comprehend it.

Mi Lan said, bewildered, "It must have been a really, really amazing essay."

The other winners also began whispering and murmuring among themselves:

"Who is this guy? Several universities are fighting over him."

"I don't know either."

"He was in the same exam room as me. When he was writing his essay, the proctor stood next to him the whole time."

"I know, his name is Chen Guiliang. I know a former winner who came to help out, and he said Chen Guiliang's essay caused a sensation among the judges. After the awards ceremony tomorrow, they're even holding a special symposium to discuss his essay!"

"A symposium? Specifically to discuss his essay?"

"That's what it sounds like. We can go and listen in, and there will be media reporters there too."

"Are they insane?"

"Damn, I was just asking at the Beida table earlier. Do you guys know what kind of offer Beida gave him?"

"What offer?"

"As long as he passes the first-tier cutoff, Beida will accept him."

"Getting into Beida with a first-tier score? Are you kidding me!"

"In the first and second years of the competition, you could get direct admission. Why can't you get into Beida with a first-tier score?"

"Tsinghua took his number too, said they'd discuss making an exception and giving him a spot after the school year starts."

"Does anyone know what he wrote?"

"I know. He wrote it in classical Chinese."

"Who told you that?"

"An alumnus who came to help out. My senior won first prize in the third competition, and this time he was responsible for proctoring Chen Guiliang's exam room."

"..."

There were only 27 Group A first-prize winners in total, and they were all gathered in this hall, so news spread exceptionally fast in private.

In less than ten minutes, everyone knew Chen Guiliang's basic situation.

At the same time, they grew even more curious. Just how good did Chen Guiliang's essay have to be to attract several famous universities to jump in and fight over him?

Hu Weishi, an editor from Mengya, stood at the entrance of the great hall, smiling.

New Concept and Mengya had a new person of interest. They had already contacted the media and could start the publicity tomorrow.

The Chen Guiliang of this moment was tied to the interests of many people and many organizations!
